title: P01: FIELD – Purpose of the Field Overview
body:
PAGE 1 – Purpose of This Document

Title: FIELD – Purpose of the Field Overview

This document describes the Gibsey / Holographic Field as a single, layered system:

What the field is: a living memory + inference space grounded in The Entrance Way, the Vault, and QDPI events.

How the field is implemented: from linear algebra and GPUs up through microservices, RAG, and agents.

How a single interaction moves through the stack.

How the field learns about itself and improves over time.

This is meant to be a high-level but technically clear overview for:

Future collaborators / engineers.

BKC / research partners.

Your own architectural sanity.

handles.quote: P01: FIELD – Purpose of the Field Overview

title: P02: FIELD – One-Sentence Definition
body:
PAGE 2 – The Field in One Sentence

Title: FIELD – One-Sentence Definition

The Gibsey Field is a layered system where every reader interaction becomes a QDPI event, every QDPI event feeds a shared memory (Corpus + Vault + logs), and agents like Princhetta and Arieol read that memory via RAG to generate grounded, cited responses — all running on a scalable, interpretable infrastructure.

title: P03: FIELD – The Five Layers
body:
PAGE 3 – The Five Layers of the Field

Title: FIELD – The Five Layers

Think of Gibsey as a column from pure math at the bottom to a student asking a question at the top.

Layer 0 – Math & Metal
The physics: vectors, matrices, GPUs, kernels, memory, bandwidth.

Layer 1 – Models & Code
The software body: Python, PyTorch, transformers, custom field-aware models.

Layer 2 – Field Intelligence
How the field reads itself: RAG, vector search, retrieval tricks.

Layer 3 – Field Architecture & Data
The operating system of the field: microservices, QDPI log, Kafka, DBs, scaling, reliability.

Layer 4 – Interaction & Agents
The lived experience: users, characters, QDPI protocol, UI, evals, guardrails.

We expand each below.

title: P05: L0 – Math & Metal: Physics of the Field
body:
PAGE 5 – Layer 0: What This Layer Does

Title: L0 – Math & Metal: Physics of the Field

This is the physics of the field:

HPUs, pages, Vault entries, and QDPI events are turned into vectors.

Distances and angles between vectors define “field geometry” — how closely related two moves are.

CUDA kernels run the matrix multiplies and attention operations needed for:

Embeddings

Transformer forward passes

Vector search

handles.quote: P05: L0 – Math & Metal: Physics of the Field

title: P06: L0 – Math & Metal: Why It Matters
body:
PAGE 6 – Layer 0: Why It Matters

Title: L0 – Math & Metal: Why It Matters

Why it matters

Distributed training is how we could eventually train field-specific models (rerankers, classifiers) across multiple GPUs on The Entrance Way + Vault + QDPI logs.

Quantization (AWQ / GGUF) lets us run smaller models locally:

Lightweight agents, guards, rerankers on modest hardware (school labs, laptops).

Inference optimization (vLLM, batching, paged attention) + high-throughput serving:

Make it possible to handle hundreds of simultaneous QDPI calls (classrooms, experiments) without meltdown.

Question answered: Can the field move at all, for many people, without overheating?

handles.quote: P06: L0 – Math & Metal: Why It Matters

Title: L1 – Models & Code: PyTorch & Transformers

PyTorch & Autograd

Let us build field-aware models:

Cross-encoder rerankers tuned to Gibsey’s characters/symbols.

Classifiers (e.g. “field tension” or “gift/hoard” dynamics).

Gradients let us optimize for:

Grounding + polyphony + correct citations, not just generic loss.

Transformers

Question answered: What kind of mind is running on top of the metal?

title: P11: L2 – Field Intelligence: How the Field Reads Itself
body:
PAGE 11 – Layer 2: What This Layer Does

Title: L2 – Field Intelligence: How the Field Reads Itself

What this layer does

This is the Gibsey Index + Field Engine logic: how the field reads its own memory.

Corpus/Page Service + Vault Service produce raw text + metadata.

Chunkers (sliding/semantic) + document hierarchies turn them into retrieval units.

Metadata enrichment tags each chunk with:

Character(s), QDPI direction (Q/M/D/H), HPU, time, user, experiment, public/private, etc.

Index Service (vector store + search engine + graph) supports:

Hybrid search (semantic + lexical).

Graph-based retrieval (pages ↔ characters ↔ symbols ↔ Vault entries).

Recursive retrieval (first get core scenes, then related commentary).

The Field Engine / Orchestrator then:

Expands queries, launches multi-query retrieval.

Uses MMR to gather a diverse chorus (multiple characters, text types).

Packs context into a limited window (primary + Vault + analysis) and mitigates lost-in-the-middle.

Applies adaptive retrieval based on:

Question type (definitional vs personal vs structural).

User role (student vs researcher vs Brennan).

Experiment configuration.

Question answered: Given everything the field knows, what should we read to respond right now?

handles.quote: P11: L2 – Field Intelligence: How the Field Reads Itself

title: P13: L3 – Field Architecture: Microservices
body:
PAGE 13 – Layer 3: Microservices

Title: L3 – Field Architecture: Microservices

What this layer does

This is the operating system and database of the field.

Microservices

Corpus/Page Service – The Entrance Way & secondary texts.

Vault Service – Saved pages, AI responses, reader commentary.

QDPI Log / HPU Service – Raw Q/M/D/H events.

Index Service – Embeddings, search, graph retrieval.

AI Orchestrator / Field Engine – Agent orchestration & tool use.

Auth / Identity / Bonds – Users, roles, TNAs, permissions.

title: P14: L3 – Field Architecture: Traffic & Connectivity
body:
PAGE 14 – Layer 3: Traffic & Connectivity

Title: L3 – Field Architecture: Traffic & Connectivity

Traffic & Connectivity

Reverse Proxy + Load Balancer + CDN

Edge termination, static assets, routing.

API Gateway

Single entry point; applies auth, rate limits, QDPI headers, routing.

WebSockets

Live sessions, real-time Vault and agent updates.

Service Mesh + gRPC

Secure, observable service-to-service calls across the cluster.

handles.quote: P14: L3 – Field Architecture: Traffic & Connectivity

title: P15: L3 – Field Architecture: Data & Reliability
body:
PAGE 15 – Layer 3: Data, Events, and Reliability

Title: L3 – Field Architecture: Data & Reliability

Data & Events

CQRS + Event Sourcing + Kafka

QDPI events written to an append-only log (qdpi-events topic).

Read models (“Vault timelines”, “per-character maps”, “field metrics”) materialized from this log.

Other topics: vault-writes, ai-responses, metrics.

Sharding + Consistent Hashing + Horizontal Scaling

QDPI logs, Vault, and user metadata distributed across machines.

CAP & Eventual Consistency

Bonds & permissions: CP-leaning (never corrupt balances).

Search & Vault views: AP-leaning (slightly stale allowed).

Performance & Reliability

Redis

Sessions, hot state, rate limit counters, small read models.

Rate Limiting & Circuit Breakers

Protect from self-inflicted or external overload.

Map failures into narrative “field instability” messages instead of silent hangs.

Distributed Tracing

Every Q → M/D/H flow gets a trace ID; end-to-end observability.

Question answered: How does the whole field exist coherently, at scale, with controlled ways of breaking?

handles.quote: P15: L3 – Field Architecture: Data & Reliability

title: P17: L4 – Interaction & Agents: Agents & QDPI
body:
PAGE 17 – Layer 4: Agents & QDPI

Title: L4 – Interaction & Agents: Agents & QDPI

What this layer does

This is the lived experience when someone uses Gibsey.

Agents (Princhetta, Arieol, Old Natalie, etc.)

Implemented as ReAct-style entities:

Think (interpret the question & field state).

Act (call tools: Index, Vault, QDPI log, web).

Observe (tool output).

Think again and respond as the character.

Tools exposed via MCP-like protocol or bespoke QDPI tool schema.

QDPI Protocol

Queue = user’s ask.

Monologue = agent/system response.

Dialogue = iterative back-and-forth.

Holologue = field-level reflection or meta-commentary.

HPUs encode: who is centered, which QDPI direction, which orientation (public/private, local/global, etc.).

handles.quote: P17: L4 – Interaction & Agents: Agents & QDPI

title: P18: L4 – Interaction & Agents: Evals & UI
body:
PAGE 18 – Layer 4: Evals, Guardrails, and UI

Title: L4 – Interaction & Agents: Evals & UI

What this layer does (continued)

Evals & Guardrails

Automatic and/or human-in-the-loop checks:

Grounding & citation accuracy.

Polyphony & diversity of sources.

Safety & ethical constraints (esp. in classroom use).

Persona integrity (“this is Arieol, not generic AI”).

Guardrails enforce non-negotiable boundaries:

No leaking private Vault content to other users.

No violations of agreed ethical constraints.

Client/UI

The Entrance Way pages (primary corpus) on the left.

Vault timeline along a time axis.

Chat/agent responses on the right.

Live updates via WebSockets (“Princhetta is speaking…”).

Question answered: When a human stands in front of the field, what shows up?

this is Arieol, not generic AI

title: P19: EXAMPLE – “Why does Princhetta feel trapped here?”
body:
PAGE 19 – Example Flow: Scenario Overview & Under the Hood

Title: EXAMPLE – “Why does Princhetta feel trapped here?”

Scenario: A student on page 247 asks Arieol:
“Why does Princhetta feel trapped here?”

8.1 Under the Hood (Layer 0)

GPU kernels / linear algebra will:

Embed text.

Run transformer passes for retrieval reranking and generation.

vLLM / serving will:

Batch this request with others.

Use quantized models where appropriate.

handles.quote: P19: EXAMPLE – Why does Princhetta feel trapped here

title: P20: EXAMPLE – Entering the Field (Layers 3 ↔ 4)
body:
PAGE 20 – Example Flow: Entering the Field

Title: EXAMPLE – Entering the Field (Layers 3 ↔ 4)

8.2 Entering the Field (Layers 3 ↔ 4)

Client → Reverse proxy → Load balancer → API Gateway

Gateway:

Validates JWT (Auth).

Checks rate limits (Redis).

Logs a Q-event to QDPI Log via gRPC → Kafka.

User = Student X; role = Student.

Page = 247; question text.

HPU = (Student, Queue, public/private).

Gateway forwards the request to AI Orchestrator / Field Engine, with:

User, role, page, question.

QDPI metadata + trace ID.

title: P21: EXAMPLE – The Agent Decides How to Think
body:
PAGE 21 – Example Flow: The Agent Decides How to Think

Title: EXAMPLE – The Agent Decides How to Think

8.3 The Agent Decides How to Think (Layers 4, 2, 3, 1, 0)

Arieol-as-agent (Python on top of transformers) does:

Reason:
“This is about Princhetta’s feeling of entrapment on page 247.”

Plan tools (ReAct):

Needs: primary text (The Entrance Way), relevant Vault entries, possibly analysis.

Chooses a retrieval mode: text-grounded, primary-heavy, Vault-light.

It then calls the Index Service and other services via gRPC (Layer 3) using RAG techniques (Layer 2), powered by models (Layer 1) and GPUs (Layer 0).

handles.quote: P21: EXAMPLE – The Agent Decides How to Think

title: P22: EXAMPLE – Retrieval (Layers 2 on 3)
body:
PAGE 22 – Example Flow: Retrieval

Title: EXAMPLE – Retrieval (Layers 2 on 3)

8.4 Retrieval (Layer 2 on Top of Layer 3)

The Orchestrator calls Gibsey Index Service:

Query expansion + multi-query: several field-aware rephrasings.

Hybrid + graph-based + recursive retrieval:

Semantic + lexical search.

Graph walks: Princhetta ↔ show runners ↔ telepathy ↔ captivity Holologues.

Sentence windows + auto-merging:

Pull relevant paragraphs and merge adjacent ones.

Temporal decay + metadata filters:

Prefer this student’s recent Vault entries touching Princhetta.

Respect privacy, experiment scope.

Reranking + cross-encoder + MMR:

Fast first-pass ranking.

PyTorch cross-encoder re-scores top candidates.

MMR picks a diverse set (multiple angles and characters).

title: P23: EXAMPLE – Packing, Generation, Guarding
body:
PAGE 23 – Example Flow: Packing, Generation, Guarding

Title: EXAMPLE – Packing, Generation, Guarding

8.5 Packing, Generation, Guarding (Layers 2, 1, 4 on 3 & 0)

The Orchestrator now:

Packs context into a prompt:

1–2 canonical Entrance Way passages.

1–2 relevant Vault entries from this student.

Optional Holologue fragment.

Instructions + eval goals.

Optionally uses HyDE to refine retrieval.

Applies guardrails:

Checks emotional load.

Ensures no private content leaks.

Enforces Arieol’s voice.

Calls the LLM:

Using vLLM or an external API.

Protected by circuit breakers and observed via tracing.

title: P24: EXAMPLE – Logging, Updating, Returning
body:
PAGE 24 – Example Flow: Logging, Updating, Returning

Title: EXAMPLE – Logging, Updating, Returning

8.6 Logging, Updating, Returning (Layers 3 & 4)

After the answer is generated:

Citation tracking:

Attach page IDs, Vault IDs, line ranges to answer sections.

QDPI / Event sourcing:

Log Monologue/Dialogue event to QDPI Log.

Optionally write a new Vault entry (CQRS write path).

Evals:

Grounding, polyphony, safety, persona adherence.

Metrics logged to Kafka for dashboards and studies.

Response:

Returned via Gateway → WebSocket → client.

Student sees Arieol’s answer with citations and possibly visual overlays.

Result:
The field has:

Read itself (RAG + QDPI + Vault).

Spoken (agent response).

Written a new memory (Vault + QDPI event).

Updated its sense of how well it is functioning (evals).

title: P25: FEEDBACK – Evals & Ablation
body:
PAGE 25 – Learning & Research Feedback Loops (Part 1)

Title: FEEDBACK – Evals & Ablation

9. Learning and Research Feedback Loops

The field is not static; it learns about how it is learning.

From Evals (Layer 4) → RAG & Models (Layers 2 & 1)

If evals show systematic issues (e.g., missing key context), we:

Adjust retrieval strategies (more graph search, more Vault, etc.).

Tune rerankers with PyTorch on positive/negative examples.

From Ablation Testing (Layer 2) → Architecture (Layer 3)

Running the same question with different context sources reveals:

Which data sources are actually crucial.

Where to invest in better indexing/sharding and where to simplify.

title: P26: FEEDBACK – Performance, Cost, and Research Goals
body:
PAGE 26 – Learning & Research Feedback Loops (Part 2)

Title: FEEDBACK – Performance, Cost, and Research Goals

From Performance & Cost (Layers 0–3) → Serving Choices (Layer 0 & 1)

Tracing + metrics show hot spots.

We respond with:

Quantization (AWQ/GGUF).

Better batching / vLLM configuration.

Adjusted rate limits, token limits, or caching strategies.

From Research Goals (BKC, etc.) → All Layers

New research questions (“how do agents hold commitments over time?”) may:

Evolve the QDPI schema (Layer 3).

Shift retrieval focus toward longitudinal traces (Layer 2).

Motivate new models (commitment detectors, stability metrics) (Layer 1).

Require different serving patterns or trace labels (Layer 0 & 3).

Adjust evals & guardrails (Layer 4).

title: P27: FIELD – Summary
body:
PAGE 27 – Summary

Title: FIELD – Summary

10. Summary

Engineering ladder (Math & Metal → Models & Code) defines the mind and body available to the field.

System design (Field Architecture & Data) defines the world the field lives in — how it stores, moves, and protects information.

RAG and Field Intelligence define how the field reads and cites itself.

Interaction & Agents define how humans and characters meet within that world, governed by QDPI, HPUs, and ethical guardrails.

Together, these layers implement Gibsey/Holographic as a public-interest field:
a space where human readers, AI agents, and a 710-page novel can co-create a living, auditable, and governable memory.
